pinev: Parcel-level: 1912 Ogle Marinette County atlas shows the family's 120 acres in S-central sec. 17 T31N R19E with a house mark, just NW of the Pelican lakes, about 5 mi W of Beaver village; the 1938 aerial shows the farmstead there (about 250 m).

1912 Marinette Co plat, Town of Beaver p. 33 (Ancestry image 31617_072129-00626): 'Gottlieb Mattrich' and 'Wm. Mattrich 80' as N-S strips in the W half of sec 17 near New Pelican Lake; 1910 census William and Marie Matrick family, Beaver. The pin (house mark and 1938 farmstead) is in that land (BLM sec 17 = 45.1539-45.1688, -88.1665..-88.1457).

src: Marinette County plat (1912), Town of Beaver p. 33 (Ancestry image 31617_072129-00626)

pinev: Farm-level: the c.1915 Hixson Grant plat (Jamestown p.94) shows 361 ac of May land in the S/W part of sec 12 T1N R2W, the section that holds Louisburg (GNIS 42.5792,-90.5557); house mark about 400 m S of Louisburg. Whether this is the 1897 farm is not proven (about 600 m).

1895 Grant Co plat, Jamestown T1N R2W p. 60 (Ancestry image 31617_072128-00173): 'Conrad May 521' in sec 12 S of Louisburg P.O.; 1900 census Conrad and Louisa May, Jamestown. So the c.1915 house mark is his farm of 1897.

src: Grant County plat (1895), Jamestown p. 60 (Ancestry image 31617_072128-00173)

pinev: Bearing-only: 3 mi SW of Palmyra from the 1927 AP story; the farm is not on the c.1915 plats (about 2.5 km).

1920 census, Palmyra Twp: Albert Blackmore (b. 1846 England, single, owns free) and brother Charley (b. 1856); the 1899 Palmyra plate and c.1915 Hixson show no Blackmore lot, so the 10 acres were bought c.1915-20 or are an unlabelled small lot; not placed.

src: US census 1920, Palmyra Twp, Jefferson Co WI (Blackmore brothers)
